## Refactoring Summary

### `Field` — `Object[][]` → `Organism[][]`
The grid was typed as `Object`, forcing every caller to cast its results. `place()` now accepts `Organism`, `getObjectAt()` returns `Organism`, and all local variables at call sites (`Animal`, `Predator`, `Scavenger`, `Prey`) were updated from `Object` to `Organism`. The dead redundant null-check inside `adjacentLocations()` (asserted on the line above) was also removed. `depth` and `width` are now `final`.

### `Entity.act()` / `Organism.giveBirth()` — `List<Entity>` → `List<Organism>`
The newborn-collection list threaded through the entire act() call chain was typed as `List<Entity>` even though only `Organism` instances are ever added to it. Changed to `List<Organism>` in the interface and all implementations, eliminating the forced `(Organism) entity` cast inside `Simulator.simulateOneStep()`.

### `Simulator` — typed list, named constants, accurate comments
`List<Entity> organisms` → `List<Organism> organisms`. Magic numbers `5` (steps/hour), `24` (hours/day), `4` (hours per time period) are now named constants. Stale fox/rabbit comments updated to reflect the current species.

### `Populator` — probability chain bug fixed + `spawn()` factories
Each `else if` branch previously drew a fresh random number, making later species geometrically less likely (lions ~5%, PoisonBerry ~2.8%). Now a single `r = rand.nextDouble()` is drawn per cell and compared against cumulative thresholds — every species gets exactly its stated probability. All eight hardcoded `new Lion(19, ...)` etc. calls are replaced with `Lion.spawn(field, location)`, removing magic food-level duplication. Each concrete class now has a `static spawn()` factory method.

### `FieldStats` / `SimulatorView` — raw `Class` types fixed
`HashMap<Class, Counter>` → `HashMap<Class<?>, Counter>`, `Map<Class, Color>` → `Map<Class<?>, Color>`, all method signatures updated. `SimulatorView.showStatus()` local variable changed from `Object` to `Organism`.

### `Organism.incrementAge()` — dead commented code removed
The `//setDead();` comment replaced by `remove()` in a prior iteration was finally deleted.
